adversary_breaks.observed: OfflineWallet.replace(...receipts:[payloadJson:"\u{FEFF}{...}"]) returns a revision-1 snapshot and writes 264 bytes to wallet.v1.<owner> (OfflineWalletShape.isJsonObject uses JSONSerialization, which tolerates a BOM). TS replaceOfflineWallet rejects with failure 'bridge_contract' (parseSnapshot -> isJsonObjectText -> JSON.parse throws) AFTER native.replaceWallet resolved; the fake native shows walletRevision 1. Every later loadOfflineWallet(owner) rejects bridge_contract, discardCorruptOfflineWallet rejects not_corrupt (native verifies fine), and clear needs the revision the caller never received.

adversary_breaks.expected: discardCorrupt must throw not_corrupt (or re-read/CAS-verify the key before deleting) and leave wallet/fence intact. Reachability: the shipping bridge uses one OfflineWallet on a serial queue, so this needs a second instance/process — but OfflineWallet.swift's own header documents exactly that multi-instance/multi-process concurrency as a supported case.
adversary_breaks.observed: readState reads key -> fence -> wallet as three non-atomic store reads. Instance B completes the owner's first replace (key+fence+wallet, receipt 'receipt-unsent') between A's key read (nil) and A's fence read. A's discardCorrupt classifies the state as integrityKeyMissing ('wallet present without its integrity key'), which satisfies isUnreadableState, and deletes wallet.v1.<owner> and fence.v1.<owner>; load afterwards returns nil — the committed receipt is gone with no error.
adversary_breaks.title: discardCorrupt racing another OfflineWallet instance's first write for the same owner deletes a healthy wallet and its fence (unsent receipt lost)

adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.expected: Either nil (pre-write view) or the revision-1 snapshot; a concurrent legitimate write must only ever be observed as wallet-ahead-of-fence, as the doc comment promises for the fence — the same reasoning must cover the key read.
adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.observed: Same interleaving as above: load throws OfflineWalletError(integrityKeyMissing, 'wallet present without its integrity key'), an outcome the TS wrapper treats as isOfflineWalletUnreadable => callers are steered to discardCorrupt.
adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.title: load racing another instance's first write is reported as integrity_key_missing (unreadable-state failure) for a healthy owner

adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.expected: clear must commit the fence to the observed wallet revision (as replace does) so revision 2 is never handed out twice and the older authentic envelope is detected as rollback. Requires a crash in the wallet->fence window plus a later Keychain restore, hence P2.
adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.observed: Wallet at revision 2, fence left at 1 (process died before commitFence). Relaunched instance: load -> revision 2 (ok), clear(expectedRevision: 2) deletes the wallet and leaves fence=1, next replace(expectedRevision: 0) returns revision 2 (expected 3). Restoring the pre-clear revision-2 envelope then loads as current state (no .tampered), although the doc comment states 'the fence survives clear, so revisions never restart for an owner on this installation'.
adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.title: clear after a crash between the wallet write and the fence commit does not repair the fence -> the next replace reuses a revision number and the pre-clear authentic envelope replays as current state

adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.expected: invalid_receipt, nothing written. Must be re-run on the Mac runner: if Apple's JSONSerialization rejects the trailing comma this entry is Linux-surrogate-only and not a shipping break.

adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.expected: Design limitation rather than a coding defect: the fence lives in the same Keychain store as the item it fences, so a whole-store restore cannot be detected without an out-of-store monotonic anchor. Reported so the 'anti-rollback' claim in the implementer summary is scoped correctly.

adversary_nonblocking_fix_if_crash_or_ch.title: Full-state rollback (wallet AND fence restored from the same earlier point) is indistinguishable from current state — anti-rollback only covers a partial restore

Design limitation (adversary P3, unchanged, by design): the fence lives in the same Keychain store as the wallet, so a restore of BOTH wallet.v1.<owner> and fence.v1.<owner> from the same earlier point (whole-store rollback) is indistinguishable from current state. Anti-rollback covers partial restores (older wallet vs newer fence) only; detecting whole-store rollback needs an out-of-store monotonic anchor (e.g. server-side revision on reconciliation).

Related: clear commits the fence to the observed revision N (not N+1) so the next replace hands out N+1 as the existing tests/adversary require; restoring the pre-clear revision-N envelope BEFORE the owner writes again therefore reads as current state (same class as the whole-store limitation). implement.summary: Defect/gap on BASE_SHA ecdd8352 (VERIFIED by `git ls-tree`): no offline wallet exists anywhere — native/vision-core/Sources has no OfflineWallet.swift, apps/mobile/ios/LocalPods/PickleNative/Sources has no PickleOfflineWallet.swift/PickleOfflineWalletBridge.m, PickleNative.podspec:13-24 lists no wallet source, and apps/mobile/src/native/ has no offlineWallet.ts, so nothing stores signed grants/unsent receipts in the Keychain and the JS side has no typed bridge. The r3 candidate (1549b6aa) was reused where sound and every prior-round finding was resolved in native/vision-core/Sources/OfflineWallet.swift: (1) BOM / trailing-comma break — r3 `OfflineWalletShape.isJsonObject` used JSONSerialization; now a strict iterative ECMA-404 scanner (`StrictJsonObjectScanner`, ~L792-988) accepts exactly what JSON.parse accepts, bounded by maxReceiptPayloadBytes=8192 and new `Limits.maxReceiptJsonDepth`=64; the TS wrapper additionally refuses such receipts with `invalid_receipt` before calling native (`refuseUnreadableReceipts`, byte length via UTF-8 count, depth via container walk with identical semantics). (2) discardCorrupt race — r3 `readState` did three non-atomic reads; now `readItems` snapshots key/fence/wallet, `classify` decides, and while the view looks corrupt it is reread until two consecutive identical reads agree (bounded by `maxStateRereads`; a view that never settles is `storage_failure`, never a discard verdict), so a concurrent first write is seen as nil or the committed revision-1 snapshot and `discardCorrupt` returns `not_corrupt` without deleting. (3) load race — same fix; `integrity_key_missing` is only reported for a stable view. (4) clear after crash in the wallet->fence window — `clear` now commits the fence to the observed wallet revision before the conditional delete (`commitFence`, which also tolerates a fence another instance already advanced), so the next replace hands out revision 3 and the pre-clear revision-2 envelope is detected as `tampered`. (5) Full-store rollback (wallet AND fence restored together) is a documented design limitation in the file header (needs an out-of-store anchor = server reconciliation); the anti-rollback claim is scoped to partial restores and no detection is claimed. implement.summary: Gap on BASE_SHA ecdd8352 (VERIFIED): no offline wallet exists in any source tree — `git grep -il offlinewallet ecdd8352` matches only .devin/program manifest/ledger records, apps/mobile/ios/LocalPods/PickleNative/Sources/ has no PickleOfflineWallet*.{swift,m}, native/vision-core has no OfflineWallet source or test, and apps/mobile/src/native/ has no wallet bridge; the only Keychain user is src/account/sessionVault.ts (react-native-keychain, session refresh credential). Signed grants and unsent receipts therefore have no device-bound, tamper-evident, atomically-replaced store. Regression tests were committed first (30532d34: native/vision-core/Tests/OfflineWalletTests.swift + apps/mobile/__tests__/offlineWalletNative.test.ts) and shown to fail on BASE_SHA (Swift: `cannot find type 'OfflineWallet' in scope`; Jest: `Cannot find module ../src/native/offlineWallet`). Implementation (761652ca): native/vision-core/Sources/OfflineWallet.swift — per owner three generic-password items in the dedicated service `com.picklesensei.offline.wallet` (kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly re-asserted on every write, kSecAttrSynchronizable=false, kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain=true): 32-byte integrity key, HMAC-signed revision fence, wallet envelope `[version][HMAC-SHA256 tag][JSON payload]` (tag binds domain, account, version, payload). `replace(ownerId, expectedRevision, contents)` validates owner/grants/receipts (≤8 grants, ≤64 receipts, compact ES256 JWS shape, strict-JSON object receipt payloads, size caps, unique ids) and writes the WHOLE wallet as one compare-and-swap Keychain operation (SecItemUpdate/SecItemDelete matched on kSecAttrGeneric = SHA-256 of the bytes last read; first write SecItemAdd → errSecDuplicateItem = conflict), then commits the fence; `load` returns nil for an absent wallet and typed `tampered` / `integrity_key_missing` / `unsupported_version` for flipped bytes, cross-owner copies, missing/garbage key, unknown versions, or an envelope behind the committed fence — never an empty wallet; `clear` needs the current revision and keeps the fence; `discardCorrupt` is the only exit from unreadable state (post-reconciliation). Errors are `OfflineWalletError{failure, detail, status}` with stable codes `wallet.<failure>`; no grant/receipt bytes are logged and no access/provider token is stored. Shipping wiring: PickleOfflineWallet.swift (RN module, one serial queue, Promise rejections carry code/message/OSStatus) + PickleOfflineWalletBridge.m (RCT_EXTERN_MODULE loadWallet/replaceWallet/clearWallet/discardCorruptWallet) compiled into the PickleNative pod via the podspec entry + Sources/Core symlink, and apps/mobile/src/native/offlineWallet.ts (typed bridge: OfflineWalletError, not_configured, bridge_contract for malformed native output, snapshot/owner/revision validation). Candidate reuses r4 (6cdd3ab9) sound work unchanged; the only r4 finding was AC1 UNKNOWN, which this lane cannot close itself (remote Mac run is coordinator-owned) — AC1 is therefore reported UNKNOWN with Linux-surrogate + provenance evidence, AC2 PASS.
